title: November Examination
instructions: This paper consists of FOUR questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Use the information provided for the accounting questions.

questions.prompt: In which economic system are decisions made mainly through supply and demand?
Which is an injection into the circular flow?
According to the law of supply, when price rises, quantity supplied…
The source document for the Debtors Journal is the…
A bakery belongs to the…
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Supplier the business owes money to
Cost that does not change with output

questions.prompt: Debtors are liabilities of the business.
The demand curve slopes downwards from left to right.
Workers in South Africa have a constitutional right to strike.
Marketing is the business function responsible for recruiting staff.
Explain why South Africa is described as a mixed economy. Give TWO examples.
questions.memo:
✓ Both the private sector and the government play a role (1)
✓ Private ownership of most businesses (1)
✓ Example 1, e.g. private banks and shops (1)
✓ Example 2, e.g. government-owned Eskom/Transnet, public schools, social grants (1)

questions.prompt: Describe the real flow and the money flow between households and businesses.
questions.memo:
✓ Households supply factors of production to businesses (1)
✓ Businesses pay income (rent, wages, interest, profit) (1)
✓ Businesses supply goods and services to households (1)
✓ Households pay for them (consumer spending) (1)

questions.prompt: At R30 per kg, consumers want 1 000 kg of tomatoes and farmers supply 1 600 kg. (a) Is there a surplus or a shortage, and how much? (b) What will happen to the price? Explain.
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ Surplus (1) ✓ of 600 kg (1)
(b) ✓ The price will fall (1) ✓ as farmers lower prices to sell unsold tomatoes, moving towards equilibrium (1)

questions.prompt: Explain THREE functions of trade unions.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): collective bargaining; protect from unfair dismissal; health and safety; represent members; educate members; influence policy

questions.prompt: Compare a command economy and a market economy by referring to ownership of resources and who makes economic decisions.
questions.memo:
✓ Command: the state owns most resources (1)
✓ Command: the government plans and decides what, how and for whom (1)
✓ Market: resources are privately owned (1)
✓ Market: decisions are made by individuals and businesses through supply, demand and prices (1)

context.text: **Bright Sparks Electrical** is a trading business that uses a mark-up of **25% on cost**. Transactions for September 2025:

items: 3 Sept: Sold goods on credit to J. Nkosi, R5 000. Invoice 210.
8 Sept: Bought trading stock on credit from Volt Wholesalers, R14 000. Invoice VW88.
18 Sept: Sold goods on credit to M. Pillay, R2 500. Invoice 211.
25 Sept: J. Nkosi paid R3 000 on her account. Receipt 044.
29 Sept: Paid Volt Wholesalers R9 000 on account. EFT 61.

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost of sales for the credit sale on 3 September.
Calculate the total of the Sales column in the Debtors Journal for September.
Name the journal in which each transaction is recorded: (a) 8 Sept, (b) 12 Sept, (c) 25 Sept, (d) 29 Sept.
questions.memo:
(a) ✓ Creditors Journal (1)
(b) ✓ Cash Receipts Journal (1)
(c) ✓ Cash Receipts Journal (1)
(d) ✓ Cash Payments Journal (1)

questions.prompt: How much does J. Nkosi owe on 30 September?
How much does the business owe Volt Wholesalers on 30 September?
For the cash sales on 12 September, give the amounts in the Bank, Sales and Cost of sales columns of the CRJ.
Show the double entry (account debited and account credited) when the Debtors Journal totals are posted to the General Ledger.
questions.memo:
✓ Debtors control debited (1) ✓ Sales credited (1)
✓ Cost of sales debited (1) ✓ Trading stock credited (1)

questions.prompt: Give ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage for Bright Sparks of selling on credit.
questions.memo:
✓ Advantage: more customers / higher sales / loyalty (1)
✓ Disadvantage: bad debts / cash-flow problems / administration (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how the Creditors Journal total for 8 September is posted to the General Ledger, and classify the Creditors control account.
questions.memo:
✓ Trading stock account debited R14 000 (1)
✓ Creditors control account credited R14 000 (1)
✓ Creditors control is a liability (1)

questions.prompt: Do a SWOT analysis for a learner who wants to start a school tuck shop, giving ONE point for each.
questions.memo:
✓ Strength, e.g. knows learners' tastes (1)
✓ Weakness, e.g. little capital / limited time (1)
✓ Opportunity, e.g. no other tuck shop / many learners (1)
✓ Threat, e.g. school rules / rising prices / competition from vendors (1)

questions.prompt: Muffins sell for R15 each and cost R6 each to make. Fixed costs are R900 per month. Calculate the break-even quantity. Show your working.
Explain FOUR functions of a business, with an example of each.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each, with example): general management; administration; financial; purchasing; production; marketing; human resources; public relations

questions.prompt: Name THREE sources of finance for a new small business.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): own savings; family/friends; bank loan; NYDA/SEDFA; investors/partners

questions.prompt: Give TWO differences between the formal and informal sectors, and explain why the informal sector is important in South Africa.
questions.memo:
✓✓ Two differences (1 each): registered vs unregistered; tax; labour laws/contracts; size
✓✓ Importance: provides income/jobs for many unemployed people (1); first step to a formal business / provides goods close to communities (1)
